html:
The Warlpiri are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Tanami Desert in the Northern Territory, northwest of Alice Springs. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. With several thousand speakers, Warlpiri is one of the largest Aboriginal languages still spoken every day.

They lived in small family groups that moved between soaks, rockholes and seasonal waters, governed by the law of the Dreaming. Their neighbours included the Ngarti and Gurindji to the north, the Warlmanpa to the northeast, the Anmatyerre to the southeast and the Pintupi to the southwest.

Contact came late but hard. After a dingo trapper was killed in 1928, a police party led reprisals now known as the Coniston massacre. The official count was 31 dead, and many historians think far more were killed. In the 1940s the government moved many Warlpiri to new settlements such as Yuendumu and Lajamanu. From the 1980s Warlpiri artists at Yuendumu became well known for their Dreaming paintings.
